name: Mosaic Neurofibromatosis Type 1

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Revised NIH Diagnostic Criteria for Neurofibromatosis Type 1 (adapted for mosaic form)

criteria.description: Presence of six or more café-au-lait macules confined to a segmental distribution
Two or more neurofibromas or one plexiform neurofibroma localized to a single body segment
Freckling in the axillary or inguinal regions limited to a segmental area
Mosaicism for NF1 gene mutation confirmed by genetic testing in affected tissue

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of two or more major criteria localized to a single body segment or mosaicism confirmed by genetic testing with one major clinical feature
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is often clinical but can be supported by genetic testing of affected tissue due to mosaicism.

pathognomonic.notes: Macules confined to a limited body region without generalized involvement
Neurofibromas localized to a specific body segment

common.symptomName: Axillary or inguinal freckling in segmental distribution
common.notes: Freckling limited to affected body segment
searchTerms: freckles in skin folds in patches

common.notes: Plexiform neurofibromas restricted to segmental areas

common.symptomName: Localized Lisch nodules in the iris
common.notes: Iris hamartomas confined to affected segment
Bone abnormalities limited to affected region

occasional.notes: Muscle involvement limited to affected segment
Cognitive impairment related to segmental CNS involvement

rare.notes: Seizures confined to affected brain regions
Spinal curvature limited to affected segment

rare.symptomName: Localized hypertension due to renal artery stenosis
rare.notes: Secondary hypertension from segmental vascular involvement
searchTerms: high blood pressure from kidney artery narrowing
localized hypertension due to renal artery stenosis

laboratory: Genetic testing demonstrating mosaic NF1 gene mutation in affected tissue
imaging: MRI or CT evidence of segmental optic pathway gliomas
X-rays showing segmental bone dysplasia or scoliosis
genetic: Postzygotic somatic NF1 gene mutation causing mosaicism
other: Histopathology of neurofibromas confirming Schwann cell proliferation

distinguishingFeatures: Generalized distribution of café-au-lait spots and neurofibromas
Germline NF1 mutation present in all cells
More systemic involvement including learning disabilities and optic gliomas

redFlags: Rapid growth or pain in neurofibromas suggesting malignant transformation
New onset neurological deficits in affected segment
Development of optic pathway glioma with visual impairment
references: Ferner RE. Neurofibromatosis 1 and neurofibromatosis 2: a twenty-first century perspective. Lancet Neurol. 2007;6(4):340-351.
Kinsler VA, et al. Segmental neurofibromatosis: clinical and molecular evidence for mosaicism. J Med Genet. 2008;45(6):377-382.
